title: PLG Signal Follow-up Playbook (SDR/AE): talk tracks, objections, persona templates, and 1/3/7/14 cadence
author: Grace O'Connor
body:
## Summary
This playbook standardizes how SDRs/AEs follow up on high-intent product-led growth (PLG) signals from Redwood Hosted API and Console usage. It provides:
- Trigger-specific talk tracks and CTAs
- Persona-based messaging (Engineering Lead, Platform/Infra, Security)
- A default 1/3/7/14-day cadence (email + call + LinkedIn), plus escalation and suppression rules
- Objection handling and handoff guidance (SE/CS)

**Outcome we want:** signals → timely, relevant outreach → qualified meeting → correct next step (Dedicated, Private, or “stay self-serve with best practices”) without harming trust.

---

## Who this is for
- **SDRs:** primary outbound owners for net-new inbound-ish PLG expansion signals
- **AEs:** take meetings, run qualification, and drive Dedicated/Private motions
- **Solutions Engineering (SE):** join when performance, reliability, architecture, or security questionnaires appear
- **Customer Success (CS):** owns expansions for CS-managed enterprise accounts (see suppression rules)

---

## Definitions
**Signal:** an internal event derived from aggregated product usage or explicit intent actions that meets a threshold and is routed into HubSpot (timeline event + tasks/sequence).

**High-intent vs. medium-intent:**
- High-intent = explicit action or repeated pain (e.g., “Contact Sales”, security questionnaire intent, repeated 429s)
- Medium-intent = directional growth/interest (e.g., spend up, region clicks) that still requires careful framing

**Golden rule:** We never imply we saw customer content, prompts, or user-level behavior. We reference **aggregated account-level patterns** or the **customer’s explicit actions**.

---

## Guardrails (trust, privacy, and compliance)
Follow these guardrails in every outbound touch:
1) **Do not reference prompt/content.** Do not mention specific user identifiers, endpoint paths that reveal sensitive product details, or named internal projects.
2) **Use ranges and “patterns” instead of exact numbers** unless the customer already discussed them (e.g., in a support ticket or previous call). Examples:
   - OK: “We’re seeing repeated rate-limit events recently”
   - OK: “Usage has been steadily increasing over the last few weeks”
   - Avoid: “You spent $12,483.22 in the last 14 days” (unless the customer shared it)
3) **Be transparent about why you’re reaching out:** “We reach out when we see scaling signals so we can help avoid reliability/cost issues.”
4) **Offer an easy out:** include a one-line opt-out in email #1 (“If not relevant, reply ‘not a priority’ and I’ll close the loop.”)
5) **Respect suppression:** if HubSpot shows an active opportunity, open support escalation, or CS-managed enterprise account, do not enroll in sequences.

If you’re unsure whether a field is safe to mention, default to **generic** and move to a discovery question.

---

## Ownership and routing (operational)
**Default owners (unless HubSpot overrides):**
- **Net-new / self-serve:** SDR-owned sequence + AE notified on high-intent
- **Existing enterprise / CS-managed:** route to **CSM/AE** per account team; SDR does not sequence

**When to pull in SE (minimum bar):**
- Dedicated conversation (throughput, concurrency, latency SLO)
- Private conversation (VPC/on-prem, procurement/security review)
- Any mention of benchmarks, kernel/runtime choices, architecture constraints, or migration concerns

**Response-time expectation (internal SLA):**
- High-intent signals: first touch within **4 business hours**
- Medium-intent signals: first touch within **1 business day**

---

## Signal → recommended motion (quick map)
Use this table to pick the right CTA and avoid over-selling.

| Signal category | What it usually means | Primary CTA | Likely next step | Who should be on the call |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Repeated 429 / rate-limit hits | Demand > current plan; reliability risk; possible misconfig | “Quick scaling review” | Hosted tuning (quotas/batching) or Dedicated | SDR + AE; add SE if repeated/painful |
| Concurrency spikes / bursty traffic | Need predictable throughput, tail-latency control | “Capacity + latency review” | Dedicated sizing / PoC | AE + SE |
| Sustained spend/usage growth | Expansion potential; may care about unit economics | “Cost/latency optimization review” | Dedicated commit or Hosted optimization | SDR + AE; SE optional |
| Error-rate / routing failures (5xx / model fallback) | Production reliability pain; needs SLO/rollback tooling | “Reliability + fallback review” | Dedicated or Hosted reliability plan | AE + SE |
| Security intent (SSO/SAML, audit logs, SOC2, security questionnaire) | Procurement/security path started | “Security + deployment options review” | Dedicated (isolation) or Private (VPC/on-prem) | AE + SE + Security as needed |
| Data residency / region constraints | Compliance or customer requirements (e.g., EU) | “Residency options review” | Dedicated in-region or Private | AE + SE |
| Repeated pricing page / “Contact Sales” | Explicit buying motion | “Book time this week” | Qualification → align offer | SDR + AE (fast handoff) |

---

## The default 1/3/7/14 cadence
**Cadence goal:** be helpful, specific, and low-friction. Each touch should add new value (benchmark, checklist, or question).

| Day | Channel | Owner | Goal | Notes |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Email #1 + (optional) LinkedIn connect | SDR | Identify the trigger category, offer a 15-min consult, include opt-out | For high-intent signals, also call same day |
| 3 | Call attempt #1 + VM + Email #2 | SDR | Create urgency; confirm pain + right owner | Keep VM non-creepy: “scaling patterns” not “we saw X tokens” |
| 7 | Email #3 (value add) + LinkedIn message | SDR | Provide concrete artifact (checklist/benchmarks) | Include 2 time slots |
| 14 | Breakup Email #4 + optional call attempt #2 | SDR | Close loop respectfully and set re-open condition | Mark outcome in HubSpot |

**Escalation (high-intent):** If signal is “Contact Sales” or “Security intent” and there’s no response by Day 3, ping AE via Slack and assign AE task in HubSpot.

**Stop conditions:** reply received, meeting booked, explicit opt-out, suppression triggered (open opp/CS-owned), or bounce.

---

## Talk tracks by signal type
Use these as *starting points*. Replace bracketed sections with what’s known from HubSpot (industry, region, general workload type).

### 1) Repeated 429 / rate-limit hits
**What they feel:** “Our app is growing and we’re hitting ceilings; latency is spiky; we can’t ship features because inference is the bottleneck.”

**Positioning:** Redwood helps teams scale without guessing: Dedicated capacity + better batching/caching + clearer SLO controls.

**Call opener (30 seconds):**
- “I’m reaching out because we’ve seen repeated rate-limit events on your Redwood usage recently. That often happens when traffic ramps faster than plan limits or batching isn’t tuned yet. If it’s useful, we can do a quick scaling review to reduce 429s and protect latency.”

**Discovery questions:**
- “Is this mostly chat generation, embeddings, or a mix?”
- “Are the spikes predictable (time-of-day) or event-driven?”
- “Do you have a latency SLO you’re trying to hit (p95/p99)?”
- “Do you have fallback logic today if a request fails or is throttled?”

**Recommended CTA:** 15–30 minute “Scaling + limits” review; if they mention hard latency/throughput needs → SE-led sizing call.

**Proof points (safe):**
- Dedicated pools for predictable throughput and isolation
- Console visibility: token-level latency/cost breakdowns + route/model dashboards
- Optimize toolkit: batching/caching suggestions to reduce unit cost while improving tail latency

---

### 2) Concurrency spikes / bursty traffic
**What they feel:** “We have launch spikes or customer-driven bursts; we can’t afford brownouts.”

**Positioning:** Dedicated is the “predictable performance” upgrade; we help define concurrency targets and success criteria.

**Talk track:**
- “When teams see bursty concurrency, the biggest risk is tail latency and throttling during peak. Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and isolation; we can also set autoscaling/burst policies depending on your pattern.”

**Discovery questions:**
- “What does ‘peak’ look like—seconds-long bursts or hours-long peaks?”
- “Is it customer-facing interactive latency, or async jobs?”
- “Do you need multi-region or a single region for compliance?”

**CTA:** “Let’s define peak concurrency + p95 target; we’ll propose a Dedicated configuration and a lightweight PoC plan.”

---

### 3) Sustained spend/usage growth
**What they feel:** “This is working, but leadership is asking about cost predictability and reliability as we scale.”

**Positioning:** We can help them reduce unit cost and de-risk scale; Dedicated commits can stabilize pricing/throughput.

**Talk track:**
- “We typically reach out when we see steady growth because it’s the best time to get ahead of cost/latency surprises. If you share your next 90-day usage expectations, we can recommend either (a) Hosted optimizations, or (b) Dedicated capacity if you want predictable throughput and pricing.”

**Discovery questions:**
- “What’s driving growth—more users, new features, or new regions?”
- “Is cost per request a KPI you track? Any target?”
- “Are you evaluating model changes/quantization, or pinned to a specific model/version?”

**CTA:** “15-min optimization review” → “30-min sizing” if they care about predictability.

---

### 4) Error-rate / model routing failures
**What they feel:** “We saw failures in production; we need reliability and clear rollback options.”

**Positioning:** Redwood is production-first: fallbacks, routing policy controls, observability, and Dedicated isolation.

**Talk track:**
- “When we see repeated error-rate spikes or routing issues, teams usually want two things: (1) a way to prevent incidents (capacity + guardrails) and (2) a safe fallback plan. We can review your current setup and propose routing/fallback patterns that reduce user-visible failures.”

**Discovery questions:**
- “Are failures correlated with peak traffic or specific regions?”
- “Do you require pinned model versions for stability?”
- “Do you have incident postmortems or error budgets we should align to?”

**CTA:** SE-supported reliability review if they have on-call pain.

---

### 5) Security intent (SSO/SAML, audit logs, SOC2, questionnaire)
**What they feel:** “We like the product, but security/procurement needs evidence and deployment controls.”

**Positioning:** Dedicated/Private align with enterprise controls: isolation, audit logs, key management, VPC/on-prem options.

**Talk track (email/call):**
- “I saw you were looking at our security/compliance resources. If you’re preparing for a security review, we can walk through the control set (SOC 2, SSO/SAML options, audit logging) and discuss deployment modes (Dedicated vs Private in your VPC) depending on requirements.”

**Discovery questions:**
- “Do you need SSO/SAML for the Console? SCIM?”
- “Any requirements around data residency, encryption/KMS, or audit log retention?”
- “Is this for your internal security team or a customer security questionnaire?”
- “Is VPC deployment required, or would Dedicated isolation satisfy policy?”

**CTA:** “30-min security + deployment options” call; bring SE; loop security approver only if needed.

**Do not do:** Don’t claim certification statuses beyond what’s in the current approved security collateral. If asked, say: “I’ll confirm the latest attestations and share the official packet.”

---

### 6) Data residency / region constraints
**What they feel:** “We’re blocked unless inference runs in-region and meets compliance.”

**Positioning:** Redwood supports dedicated capacity in specific regions and Private deployments for regulated workloads.

**Talk track:**
- “If your customers require EU-only processing (or similar residency), we can outline which regions are supported for Hosted vs Dedicated, and what Private (VPC/on-prem) looks like if you need stricter controls.”

**Discovery questions:**
- “Is the requirement contractual (DPA) or internal policy?”
- “Is it just inference, or also logs/telemetry retention?”

**CTA:** AE + SE to confirm region support and propose path.

---

### 7) Repeated pricing page visits / “Contact Sales”
**What they feel:** “We’re evaluating options and need pricing/packaging clarity.”

**Positioning:** Make it easy: clarify packages, avoid a long discovery gate, and propose the smallest next step.

**Talk track:**
- “Happy to help you compare options quickly. Are you mostly looking for predictable throughput (Dedicated), security/residency controls (Private), or just a better unit cost on Hosted?”

**CTA:** Book meeting within the week; handoff to AE same day for “Contact Sales.”

---

## Persona-based messaging frameworks
Pick the persona based on title + what they respond to. If in doubt, start with Engineering Lead framing.

### A) Engineering Lead / Product Engineering (VP Eng, Eng Manager, Tech Lead)
**Cares about:** shipping, reliability, latency SLO, incident load, developer experience

**Angles that land:**
- “Protect p95/p99 latency as traffic ramps”
- “Avoid rate-limit surprises and incidents”
- “Pin versions + rollouts (canary/fallback) to reduce regressions”

**Good questions:**
- “What does ‘good enough latency’ mean for your feature?”
- “Any upcoming launches or customer deadlines?”
- “What’s your plan for graceful degradation when capacity is constrained?”

**Best CTA:** 15-min review → SE deep dive if SLO-driven.

---

### B) Platform / Infra / ML Platform (Platform Eng, SRE, ML Infra)
**Cares about:** predictability, unit economics, scaling controls, observability, architecture fit

**Angles that land:**
- “Dedicated capacity = predictable throughput + isolation”
- “Cost/perf levers: batching, caching, quantization profiles, routing policy”
- “Operational tooling: per-route dashboards, tracing hooks, error analysis”

**Good questions:**
- “What’s the traffic shape and concurrency target?”
- “Do you need multi-region routing/failover?”
- “Are you measuring tokens/sec, cost/request, or both?”

**Best CTA:** 30-min architecture + sizing call with SE.

---

### C) Security / Compliance / Procurement (Security Eng, GRC, IT)
**Cares about:** risk, controls, auditability, identity, data handling, residency

**Angles that land:**
- “Deployment options: Dedicated isolation vs Private in VPC/on-prem”
- “Audit logs + access controls + key management integrations”
- “Clear retention and acceptable-use posture”

**Good questions:**
- “Do you require SSO/SAML for admin access?”
- “Any hard requirements for VPC, HSM/KMS, or audit log retention?”
- “What’s the procurement timeline and who signs off?”

**Best CTA:** security review + deployment options call; do not overspec; offer official security packet.

---

## Templates (copy blocks)
**Personalization tokens (use what’s available in HubSpot):**
- {{first_name}}, {{company}}, {{role}}, {{region}}, {{use_case}}, {{workload_type}} (chat/embeddings), {{meeting_link}}, {{ae_name}}

### Email #1 (Day 1) — Rate-limit / scaling pain
**Subject options:**
- “Quick scaling check-in for {{company}} (avoiding 429s)”
- “Reducing throttling + protecting latency as you scale”

**Body:**
Hi {{first_name}},

Reaching out because we’ve seen repeated rate-limit events on your Redwood usage recently. That often shows up when traffic ramps quickly or batching/caching settings haven’t been tuned for peak.

If helpful, I can grab 15 minutes to:
- sanity-check your peak concurrency + latency targets
- share a few low-effort ways teams reduce 429s and tail latency
- outline when Dedicated capacity makes sense for predictable throughput

Would {{time_option_1}} or {{time_option_2}} work?

If this isn’t a priority, just reply “not a priority” and I’ll close the loop.

— {{sender_name}}

### Email #1 (Day 1) — Security intent
**Subject options:**
- “Security review help (Dedicated vs Private options)”
- “{{company}} + Redwood security/compliance questions”

**Body:**
Hi {{first_name}},

Noticed you were looking at our security/compliance resources. If you’re preparing for a security review, we can walk through the control set (e.g., audit logging, SSO/SAML options) and discuss deployment modes (Dedicated vs Private in your VPC) depending on your requirements.

Are you the right person for security review coordination? If not, who should I loop in?

If you’re open to it, I can do a 20–30 minute review this week: {{meeting_link}}

— {{sender_name}}

### Email #2 (Day 3) — Value + direct question
**Subject:** “Worth a quick look?”

Hi {{first_name}},

Quick follow-up—when teams hit scaling friction, the fastest unblock is usually answering two questions:
1) What peak concurrency + p95 latency do you need?
2) Do you prefer to solve it via Hosted tuning, or do you need Dedicated for guaranteed throughput/isolation?

If you reply with (a) your rough peak and (b) your target latency, I’ll suggest the right next step (and pull in an SE if needed).

— {{sender_name}}

### Email #3 (Day 7) — Artifact offer
**Subject:** “Checklist: Dedicated readiness (5 mins)” 

Hi {{first_name}},

If it’s useful, I can share a short checklist we use to scope a Dedicated PoC:
- traffic shape (steady vs bursty)
- model/version pinning needs
- required regions/residency
- success criteria (p95/p99 + throughput)

Want me to send it, or would you prefer a quick walkthrough?

— {{sender_name}}

### Email #4 (Day 14) — Breakup
**Subject options:**
- “Close the loop?”
- “Should I stop reaching out?”

Hi {{first_name}},

I don’t want to spam you. Should I close this out for now?

If scaling/performance/security becomes a priority later, reply with “revisit” and I’ll re-open and route you to the right team.

— {{sender_name}}

---

## Objection handling (quick responses)

### “We’re fine on self-serve / not a priority.”
**Response:**
- “Makes sense. If it becomes relevant, we can do a fast review focused on (a) preventing throttling and (b) keeping latency stable. I’ll close the loop—okay to check back in a month or two?”

### “We’re just exploring / doing research.”
**Response:**
- “Totally fair. Would a 10-minute comparison between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private be useful, or should I just send a short summary?”

### “We don’t want to talk to sales.”
**Response:**
- “Understood—this isn’t a sales pitch. The goal is to help you avoid reliability/cost surprises as you scale. If after 15 minutes there’s nothing to do, we’ll end it there.”

### “We’re concerned about cost.”
**Response:**
- “That’s exactly when we should talk—Dedicated can improve cost predictability, and Hosted tuning (batching/caching/routing) often reduces unit cost without changing your app. If you share your traffic shape, we can recommend the lowest-effort path.”

### “We need EU-only / residency / strict compliance.”
**Response:**
- “We can walk through region support and what Dedicated vs Private looks like for your constraints. If you tell me your hard requirements, I’ll bring the right people and keep it focused.”

### “We already have a vendor / we’re comparing providers.”
**Response:**
- “Makes sense. If you share your top 2 criteria (latency, cost, security, residency, ops), we can show you how Redwood addresses them and where we’re not the best fit.”

---

## Handoff and next steps
**If they say yes to meeting:**
1) Book on AE calendar (or SDR if you run qualification first).
2) Add SE if any of: Dedicated sizing, Private/VPC, security questionnaire, concurrency/latency benchmarks.
3) Add a 3-bullet agenda in the invite:
   - workload + traffic shape
   - target latency/throughput + current pain
   - recommended deployment mode + next step

**If they mention an active incident/support escalation:**
- Pause outbound and coordinate with Support/CS. A “help-first” approach wins here.

**If it’s clearly CS-managed expansion:**
- Assign to CSM and add a note: signal type + customer impact summary. Do not run SDR sequence.

---

## HubSpot hygiene (required)
Log outcomes so scoring/threshold tuning improves:
- **Outcome:** Meeting booked / Not now / Not a fit / Opt-out / No response
- **Primary trigger:** Rate-limit / Concurrency / Spend growth / Security / Residency / Pricing intent
- **Notes:** customer-stated pain, timing, stakeholder roles, and any compliance constraints

**If you see duplicate tasks or repeated enrollments:**
- Stop outreach and flag in #help-bizsystems with the HubSpot record link. (Duplicates were a known early pilot failure mode; we prefer one clean thread.)

---

## FAQ
**Q: Can I mention exact usage/spend numbers?**
A: Default is **no** (use patterns/ranges). Only use exact numbers if the customer provided them first or it’s explicitly approved for that account/context.

**Q: What if they ask “how did you know?”**
A: “We monitor aggregated account-level usage patterns so we can proactively help customers avoid scaling issues. We do not look at prompt content.”

**Q: What’s the best single question to qualify Dedicated?**
A: “What peak concurrency and p95 latency do you need, and what happens if you miss it?”

**Q: When do we recommend Private vs Dedicated?**
A: Private when they require customer-managed networking (VPC/on-prem), stricter auditability/key management constraints, or regulated/air-gapped needs. Dedicated when they primarily need predictable performance, isolation, and enterprise controls without full private control plane requirements.
